title: Paused campaigns on a write-denied target, migration controls, jobloop backoff, step-up cookie
kind: code slice, not an acceptance run — nothing here is lab-observed

closes.a34_finding_1: a migration target the process cannot write to is a fatal boot refusal, for the api AND the workers
closes.a34_finding_2: an anonymous read during a PostgreSQL outage answers a bare 500 internal_error where the authenticated path is typed
closes.a34_finding_3: internal/jobloop has no backoff ladder — every loop retries at its fixed tick for the whole outage
closes.a34_finding_4: a campaign whose objects are failing shows objects_failed 0 and last_error '' until the attempt budget is spent; the failure categories are projected nowhere
closes.a34_finding_5: the storage-migration WARN redacts object_key and then prints the same key verbatim inside the error string beside it
closes.a34_finding_6: storage_migrations job_runs rows carry empty correlation_id/request_id/worker_id
closes.a34_finding_8: an aborted campaign's partial copies stay on the destination forever; nothing in the product removes them
closes.a34_finding_9: the GC refusal during cutover reports bucket_ownership before storage_migration_active
closes.auth_rehearsal_finding: the step-up query token appears in the proxy's Referer lines, where the identically-shaped mfa_token does not

not_closed.a34_finding_7: vidra-user cannot start or cancel a storage migration — CLOSED by this slice's user PR, listed here only because A34 wrote it as a separate line from finding 4

vidra-core.scope: migration 0145, the pause rail, the control surface, the three SC3 fixes, the step-up cookie, OpenAPI

vidra-user.scope: StorageMigrationControls, the api wrappers, SecureAccountSection's transport change, lib/api/generated.ts regen
vidra-user.ordering: DRAFT UNTIL core#226 MERGES; the contract lane regenerates against that PR's openapi.yaml and cannot be green before it

sc1_paused_campaigns.ruling: a write-denied migration TARGET must not be a boot refusal; only the AUTHORITATIVE store being write-denied stays fatal
sc1_paused_campaigns.what_it_replaced: boot with a read-only target credential printed `fatal error="storage migration target: ... Access Denied. [write_denied]"` and the process exited BEFORE the listener opened — /healthz answered nothing at all, for the api as well as the workers

boot_now.handle: kept — newMigrationTargetBackend builds the backend without EnsureBucket when the bucket check is refused with class write_denied; every OTHER class stays fatal
boot_now.probe: storage.NewWriteHealth on the TARGET, boot sample taken synchronously (RecordDenied when the bucket check already answered, so no second round trip), then its own storage.WriteProbeInterval = 5 min ticker in EVERY role
boot_now.readiness: 200. The `storage` component reads `degraded` with the class — never `down`, because the store this instance SERVES from is fine and it is the MOVE that has stopped
boot_now.authoritative_store: unchanged. blobs' own EnsureBucket failure is still fatal and its own boot write probe is still non-fatal-but-degrading, exactly as the Storage hardening slice left them

pause.resume_state: the phase the campaign came out of, so a resume never guesses — a campaign paused out of synced is ready to cut over and one paused out of copying is not
pause.set_by: Service.reconcileTargetWritability, at the top of every SweepOnce, before anything reads a store
pause.auto_resume: the same function, when the probe turns positive again. An OPERATOR pause is never lifted there — an admin who paused a move for a maintenance window must not find it running again five minutes later
pause.start_refuses: Start answers ErrTargetWriteDenied (409) rather than creating a campaign that would park on its first tick
pause.resume_refuses: Resume answers ErrTargetWriteDenied (409) rather than resuming a campaign the next sweep would pause again within the minute
pause.single_active_index: untouched. paused and aborting are both LIVE by storage_migrations_single_active_idx's predicate, so neither lets a second campaign start — VERIFIED against live PostgreSQL 16.15 (a second INSERT with state='paused' beside an 'aborting' row was refused: duplicate key on storage_migrations_single_active_idx)

tests: TestAWriteDeniedTargetPausesTheCampaign — pause, reason, resume_state, the operator sentence, CopyOnce claims zero, the source keeps every object
TestARecoveredTargetResumesTheCampaign — the probe recovers and the campaign finishes with no operator action
TestAnOperatorPauseSurvivesAHealthyProbe — and an explicit Resume finishes it

sc2_migration_controls.all_routes: admin-only (requireAuth + requireRole(admin)) and audited through one shared helper, so a control cannot be added without an audit row
sc2_migration_controls.audit_content: campaign id, the resulting state, and COUNTS only. A refusal records a short category (illegal_transition state=<state>, target_write_denied, cutover_not_observed, objects_uncopied), never the error's own sentence, which can name a store

transitions.resume: paused -> resume_state (or copying when it names nothing)
transitions.abort: enumerating | copying | synced | paused -> aborting -> cancelled (with clean-up); anything non-terminal -> cancelled (without)
transitions.switch: copying | synced -> cutover, AND the topology must already be SWAPPED
transitions.release: cutover -> deleting_source, AND every object must be accounted for

sc2_migration_controls.illegal_transition: 409 NAMING the state the campaign is actually in, re-read from the row rather than echoed from the caller — the commonest cause is a stale page
sc2_migration_controls.guards: every control is a guarded UPDATE whose ROWCOUNT decides, never a read-then-write, so it is safe against the sweep worker changing the same row on its own clock. The in-memory fake mirrors each predicate exactly

dry_run.creates: nothing — no campaign row, no ledger row, no write to the target
dry_run.returns: both store identities, the exact object count, and the byte total
dry_run.bytes: storage.SizedRootLister, a new optional capability both shipped backends satisfy at no extra cost (the local walk already holds a DirEntry it can Info(); an S3 list response already carries every object's size). bytes_known is false rather than a zero when a backend cannot answer cheaply

abort_cleanup.why_a_state: a campaign aborted at 90% has hundreds of thousands of objects to remove and an admin request must not hold a connection open for them
abort_cleanup.who: the LEADER-GATED sweep, in batches of 200 — the same rail, the same batch size and the same interruptibility as the delete-source phase at the other end of a successful move
abort_cleanup.which_objects: only rows in state 'verified' — a row that never reached that state was never confirmed to be on the destination, and a delete for a key whose copy might not be ours is the mistake this package exists to prevent
abort_cleanup.identity_assertion: Describe(s.target) == campaign.target_desc, repeated at the batch even though the caller established the topology, exactly as deleteSourceBatch does — inverted
abort_cleanup.refused_after_cutover: the destination is then the store the api SERVES from; the api refuses it and the UI does not offer the button
abort_cleanup.confirmation: typed PURGE in the body (422 without it) and arm-then-type in the UI — the media-GC page's word and doctrine, unchanged

switch_and_release.switch: RECORDS a cutover the operator has already performed in the environment. It cannot perform one — which store a process serves from is decided by the environment it started with — so a forward topology answers 409 cutover_not_observed saying which half of the two-step action is missing. What it buys over the leader sweep is immediacy: the sweep observes cutover on a 1-minute ticker (A34 measured 60 s), this answers at once, either way
switch_and_release.release: ends the grace window early. Until now the only way to express that was to edit STORAGE_MIGRATION_GRACE_HOURS and restart — a config change to express a one-off intent, on a running instance, mid-migration. The precondition that cannot be waived (every object accounted for) is RE-CHECKED here rather than trusted from the counters
switch_and_release.two_steps: release is reachable only from cutover, never as a consequence of switch. It is the act that makes the move irreversible

failure_categories.finding: objects_failed counts only rows whose whole five-attempt budget is spent, so a campaign every object of which is being refused reports 0 failed and an empty last_error for as long as the backoff ladder takes — the operator watches progress stall and is told nothing
failure_categories.query: CountStorageMigrationObjectFailuresByCategory — GROUP BY last_error, splitting terminal from retrying
failure_categories.surface: the single-campaign read (GET .../{id}) carries `failures`, and the admin page renders it as a table. The list omits it, as it omits `objects`
failure_categories.safety: the category column has been a short FIXED vocabulary since 0107 precisely so it could be projected; it never carries a key, an endpoint or a raw backend error

frontend.component: components/StorageMigrationControls.tsx, hosted by AdminInfrastructureView's Storage panel
frontend.session: the campaign-DETAIL read is viewer-scoped and goes through useSettledSession (settled + viewerKey), so it is not fired before the access token is redeemed from the httpOnly refresh cookie
frontend.state_vocabulary: MIGRATION_STATE_LABEL/VARIANT stay exhaustive Records over the contract union, so a phase added core-side is a type error rather than a raw snake_case string on the page — which is exactly what happened when paused and aborting arrived
frontend.honesty: the card SAYS cutover is an environment change the page cannot make, instead of that being the unexplained reason there are no buttons

jobloop_backoff.shape: per PASS, not per loop: a failing sweep cannot silence the drain beside it
jobloop_backoff.ladder: retry.Backoff(consecutive_failures, Interval, DefaultBackoffMax) — base x 2^n, capped
jobloop_backoff.cap: DefaultBackoffMax = 10 minutes, overridable per Loop via BackoffMax
jobloop_backoff.first_failure: costs NO extra delay — Backoff(1, ...) is the interval itself, so one bad tick is not treated as an outage
jobloop_backoff.reset: on the first success, so a flaky dependency that works one tick in three never climbs
jobloop_backoff.log: the WARN moved from Pass.run up to Loop.Run (only the loop knows how far up the ladder a failure is) and now carries consecutive_failures and retry_in. A recovery logs `job loop pass recovered` with after_failures, so the last line in the log is never a failure
jobloop_backoff.measured_before: A34 sampled the same WARN at exactly 10.000 s apart for a whole PostgreSQL outage, scaling with workers x loops

anonymous_database_outage.before: an AUTHENTICATED request answered a typed 503 session_store_unavailable; an ANONYMOUS read of the same instance answered a bare 500 internal_error
anonymous_database_outage.now: 503 database_unavailable, from pgconv.IsUnavailable in the central error handler, placed LAST so any service that already turned a driver error into a domain answer keeps it
anonymous_database_outage.why_narrow: those mean the database ANSWERED. Calling them unavailable would turn a slow query into a dependency outage on the status page and tell a client to retry a request that will fail the same way
anonymous_database_outage.leak_check: the tests assert the response body carries no host, port, user or driver sentence

redaction.the_leak: the WARN redacted object_key to [redacted-key] and printed the same key verbatim inside `"error", err.Error()` beside it — `storage: s3: put "thumbnails/<uuid>.jpg": Access Denied`
redaction.why_it_is_the_default_shape: a backend error names the key it failed on almost by definition, so an unredacted error string beside a redacted key is the normal case rather than an unlucky one
redaction.guard_extension: TestObjectKeyLogValuesAreRedacted now requires that when a log call names a storage key, the PROSE fields in the SAME call (error, reason, detail, cause, path) are redacted too. Conditional on purpose: an `error` on a mail-relay line names a host, not a key, and redacting it would cost an operator the sentence they need
redaction.helper: jobstatus.RedactError — RedactDetail for an error value, nil-safe

storage_migration_identity.finding: storage_migrations IS projected into job_runs (the 0107 trigger), so A17's 'does not call the job recorder yet' list is stale for this queue — but the projected rows carried EMPTY request_id/correlation_id/worker_id
storage_migration_identity.columns: on the QUEUE ROW (storage_migrations), not only on the projection, because the queue row is what survives — the 0139 reasoning verbatim
storage_migration_identity.written_by: CreateStorageMigration, from observability.CorrelationFromContext, so the campaign names the admin request that started it; worker_id is stamped by whichever worker is driving it (processheartbeat.SelfID, the same string jobtrace uses)
storage_migration_identity.carried_by: a SECOND trigger, storage_migrations_run_identity, which sorts after storage_migrations_operational_projection alphabetically so the run exists by the time it fires. Guarded on the existing value, so a later empty-identity update cannot erase what the start recorded
storage_migration_identity.verified_live: on PostgreSQL 16.15 at schema 145 — UPDATE storage_migrations SET request_id/correlation_id/worker_id produced job_runs 'req-fixture-1 / corr-fixture-1 / host-fixture:9'

gc_interlock_order.before: a destructive POST /admin/media/gc DURING cutover reported forced_reason=bucket_ownership, because a campaign stamps the destination's ownership marker as its LAST act, so mid-move the destination legitimately carries no marker and the ownership gate fired first
gc_interlock_order.now: the migration interlock is evaluated first and names storage_migration_active
gc_interlock_order.outcome_unchanged: both rails refuse the same sweep and deleted stays 0 either way. Only the SENTENCE changes, and 'a migration is running' is the cause where an unadopted destination mid-move is one of its symptoms
gc_interlock_order.bonus: the ownership branch re-reads the marker OUT OF THE STORE before it forces a dry run; a sweep already blocked by a live campaign no longer pays for that round trip
gc_interlock_order.test: TestMigrationReasonWinsOverTheOwnershipCheck (was TestOwnershipReasonWinsOverTheMigrationCheck, inverted) plus TestOwnershipStillNamesItselfWithNoMigration, which pins that the ownership rail is still live

sc4_step_up_transport.measured_cost_of_the_query: the auth rehearsal put a real logging Caddy proxy in front of the flow: `step_up=<32 bytes>` appears in its access log and in the `Referer` of every same-origin subresource the landing page fetches, while `vidra_mfa_pending` — the same shape of secret, one route away — appears in 0 access-log lines, 0 Referer headers and 0 browser history entries, because the proxy logs "Cookie":["REDACTED"]

cookie.name: vidra_step_up
cookie.why_that_path: the narrowest prefix BOTH consumers share — POST /auth/me/password/set and POST /auth/me/email-change. Not '/': a cookie that rides requests it cannot authorise is a cookie in more logs than necessary, which is the finding
cookie.samesite: Lax — it must survive the top-level GET back from the provider
cookie.ttl: auth.StepUpTTL = 10 minutes, the same constant the row uses, exported so the two cannot drift
cookie.single_use: the ROW is spent by the statement that reads it; the cookie is cleared on success and whenever the token turns out to be missing, spent, expired or another session's

sc4_step_up_transport.landing_url: return_to UNCHANGED — typically /settings/security?secure=password. No token AND no flag beside it: the page shows the form it was asked for, and an absent assertion is answered by the route as 403 step_up_required, which the page already renders. step_up and step_up_error are both stripped from the redirect on success
sc4_step_up_transport.row_binding: the fix from core#225 is untouched — the assertion still survives the refresh rotation the redirect causes
sc4_step_up_transport.body_field: step_up_token survives as OPTIONAL, for an API client with no cookie jar. The COOKIE wins when both are present, so a stale token in a body cannot outrank a fresh grant
behaviour_changes_worth_naming: POST /auth/me/password/set with no assertion is now 403 step_up_required rather than 422 — a browser's request carries no such field, and a validation error naming one is an instruction the page cannot follow
/auth/me/email-change moved its exactly-one-proof rule out of Validate and into the handler, the only place that can see the cookie
sc4_step_up_transport.frontend: SecureAccountSection reads NO token, from the URL or anywhere else. `?secure=` is a flag that can only be on the URL because a callback redirected to a return_to the page built, so its presence at mount is what distinguishes a completed round trip from someone opening settings; a failed one carries ?step_up_error= instead and does NOT unlock the form
tests: core: the shared callback helper asserts the Location carries no step_up=, that the ONLY query parameter is `secure`, and that the cookie is httpOnly + SameSite=Lax + Path=/api/v1/auth/me
core: TestStepUpCookieAloneAuthorises — a body naming no token, cookie only, 204, the cookie cleared, and the same cookie refused on replay
user: unlocks the form from the flag alone with no token in the URL; does not unlock when the round trip failed; both writes send bodies without step_up_token

migration.name: storage_migration_pause_and_identity
migration.check_widened: storage_migrations_state_check, by the drop-then-re-add-the-same-name idiom scripts/migrate-lint.sh allows — widening a CHECK cannot invalidate a row that already satisfied the narrower one

projection.paused: job_runs state retry_scheduled, stage paused — the run is not waiting to START, it started and will continue
projection.aborting: job_runs state cancel_requested, stage aborting — the cancel is accepted and the work of cancelling is still running

migration.down: reversible with LIVE ROWS: a paused campaign is put back into the state its resume_state names (copying when it names none) and an aborting one becomes cancelled BEFORE the CHECK narrows, so the constraint can never fail against real data
migration.verified_live: native PostgreSQL 16.15 on 55931, migrated from empty to 145, then down and up again with a paused campaign in the table — state came back as 'synced' (its resume_state), all five columns dropped and returned, and both new projections re-checked

unverified: Every claim in this file is from unit and integration tests plus a live native PostgreSQL, and NOT lab-observed. No process was booted against a real write-denied bucket, so 'boot succeeds and readiness stays 200' is asserted by the health-component unit test and the boot code path, not measured

The ABORT CLEAN-UP has removed objects only from a LOCAL backend. It has no S3-backed integration case of its own, so the one new destructive path in this slice is the one an object store has not seen
The admin page was never opened in a browser — the controls are proved by component tests against the regenerated contract
